# Path syntax

Which units separate segments on this system, and the prefix and root a path opens with.

<h2 id="is-separator"><code>IsSeparator</code></h2>

```rux
pub func IsSeparator(unit: OsUnit) -> bool
```

Whether `unit` separates path segments on this system.
Both slashes on Windows, the forward one alone elsewhere.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Path/Src/Path.rux#L17)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type     | Description      |
| ------ | -------- | ---------------- |
| `unit` | `OsUnit` | the unit to test |

**Returns**: whether the unit separates components on this system

<h2 id="preferred-separator"><code>PreferredSeparator</code></h2>

```rux
pub func PreferredSeparator() -> OsUnit
```

The separator this system prefers when one has to be written.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Path/Src/Path.rux#L29)

**Returns**: the separator this system writes, which is not the only one it accepts

<h2 id="prefix-kind"><code>PrefixKind</code></h2>

```rux
pub enum PrefixKind: int32 {
    None = 0,
    Drive = 1,
    Share = 2,
    Verbatim = 3
}
```

The kind of prefix a path opens with.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Path/Src/Prefix.rux#L14)

**Cases**

| Name       | Value | Description                                            |
| ---------- | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `None`     | `0`   | No prefix: the path is a plain name, rooted or not.    |
| `Drive`    | `1`   | A drive, `C:`, with or without a root after it.        |
| `Share`    | `2`   | A UNC share, `\server\share`.                          |
| `Verbatim` | `3`   | The verbatim prefix `\?\` and everything it qualifies. |

<h2 id="prefix-length"><code>PrefixLength</code></h2>

```rux
pub func PrefixLength(path: Path, kind: *var PrefixKind) -> uint
```

How many units of `path` are prefix, and which kind, reported through `kind`.
Zero and `None` on the Unix systems always: a leading `//server` is just a path there, whatever tools make of
it. On Windows the drive is two units, a share runs through the end of its share name, and the verbatim prefix
covers its four units plus the drive or share inside it.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Path/Src/Prefix.rux#L33)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type              | Description                  |
| ------ | ----------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `path` | `Path`            | the path to act on           |
| `kind` | `*var PrefixKind` | which prefix form to measure |

**Returns**: how many leading units the prefix occupies, or zero when there is none

<h2 id="has-root"><code>HasRoot</code></h2>

```rux
pub func HasRoot(path: Path) -> bool
```

Whether `path` has a root: a separator standing where the segments begin.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Path/Src/Prefix.rux#L106)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type   | Description        |
| ------ | ------ | ------------------ |
| `path` | `Path` | the path to act on |

**Returns**: whether the path begins at a root

<h2 id="is-absolute"><code>IsAbsolute</code></h2>

```rux
pub func IsAbsolute(path: Path) -> bool
```

Whether `path` names one place regardless of any current directory.
On the Unix systems, rooted is absolute. On Windows a rooted drive (`C:\x`), a share and a verbatim path are
absolute; `C:name` is drive-relative and `\name` drive-absent, and neither names one place on its own.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Path/Src/Prefix.rux#L123)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type   | Description        |
| ------ | ------ | ------------------ |
| `path` | `Path` | the path to act on |

**Returns**: whether the path names a location without needing a working directory
